title: Annotatio V §.XI: receiving Eucharist ≠ oral eating body; incorruptibility ≠ corporeal feeding
pass_a_gloss: So also they profess that our bodies — i.e. of the faithful — both receive the Eucharist (i.e. the Eucharistic bread) and, receiving, are no longer merely corruptible but have hope of resurrection to eternal life. But it is one thing for the faithful’s bodies to receive the Eucharist; another to eat Christ’s body with the mouth of the body. Again: one thing that bodies receiving the Eucharist are not (merely) corruptible or to remain in death but have resurrection hope; another (as the Author interprets Irenaeus) that our corruptible bodies are nourished and fed by Christ’s incorruptible body and blood and thereby made incorruptible.
pass_b_english: They also teach the faithful’s bodies receive the Eucharistic bread and, receiving, hold resurrection hope — no longer merely corruptible.

But receiving the Eucharist ≠ orally eating Christ’s body; and resurrection hope for receivers ≠ the Author’s reading that corruptible bodies are fed into incorruption by Christ’s incorruptible body and blood.
source_text: Sic etiam corpora nostra, i.e. fidelium, tam Eucharistiam, i.e. panem Eucharisticum, percipere, quàm percipientia, jam non amplius corruptibilia esse, sed spem resurrectionis ad vitam æternam habentia, profitentur. At aliud est, corpora fidelium Eucharistiam percipere; aliud, Ore corporis, corpus Christi manducare; Iterúmque: aliud, corpora fidelium Eucharistiam percipientia, non corruptibilia esse, vel, in morte mansura, sed spem resurrectionis habere; aliud (quomodo Autor Irenæum interpretatur) corpora nostra corruptibilia, corpore & sanguine Christi incorruptibilibus, nutriri & ali, hôcque pacto incorruptibilia fieri.

lemmas.gloss: to eat Christ’s body with the body’s mouth
